To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the artificial plasma disturbances in the ionosphere, generated by SURA heating, can be observed by the SWARM satellites on heights ∼450 km and ∼500 km.
The measurements were carried in 2016, the heights were ∼450 km and 500 km, and the disturbances were caused by powerful radio wave radiation.

(1) the measurements of electron density, carried out by the SWARM satellites, show the presence of artificial disturbances of the ionosphere, generated by the SURA heating facility, in the height range 450–500 km, which are in good agreement with the data of ground-based observations of the same disturbances, (2) the measurements of the electron temperature, also carried out by the satellites, show the appearance of a local increase of the electron temperature in the height range ∼450 km
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: the influence of artificial plasma disturbances on the electron density and the electron temperature, the influence of the geomagnetic activity on the artificial plasma disturbances.
a comparison of the electron density and electron temperatures measured in the ionosphere, which was disturbed by the powerful radio wave, with the data obtained in the undisturbed ionosphere region.
the following questions: 1) How do the electron density and electron temperatures of the ionosphere region vary in the area of the heating facility?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the artificial plasma disturbances at 450 km height were observed in the region of the ionospheric F-layer, and at 500 km height they were observed in the ionospheric D-region.
the electron density disturbances, caused by the radio wave, are observed in the ionosphere region at the heights ∼500 km.

the artificial disturbances of the plasma density and temperature, which were registered by the on-board instruments of Swarm satellites in the ionosphere region during the SURA heating facility operation, were caused by the radio wave radiated at a frequency of 8.1 MHz, which corresponds to the fundamental frequency of the ionospheric cavity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the artificial disturbances are observed in the electron density and temperature at the heights about 500km and that these changes are associated with the changes of ionospheric parameters in the F region.
the electron temperature in the ionosphere region under study was found to be in the range of 500-1000 K.
the artificial plasma disturbances, caused by powerful radio waves, are characterized by the presence of a number of features, which can be used for identification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
artificial plasma disturbances are clearly seen at the height ∼500 km, where the density of the ionosphere plasma is much smaller than at lower altitudes.
the heating of the ionosphere leads to a significant increase in electron density at heights of ∼450 km and a slight increase in electron density and electron temperate at heights of ∗500 km.
the electron density disturbances, caused by the heating, were detected at the heights about 450–500 km.
